reviewer: Captain (A-lane source and form-identity determination; not a counsel approval)
theBoundedQuestion: What is the correct filing vehicle for C.G.S. § 54-142a(f)(2), the petition for misdemeanor convictions committed while the person was under eighteen where the offense occurred before January 1, 2000?

answer.inOneSentence: JD-CR-202 is the Clean Slate pre-2000 petition and its own instruction forbids using it for anything else, so it is not the § 54-142a(f)(2) vehicle; and no current authoritative source read here establishes what the (f)(2) vehicle is, so the branch stays blocked.

part1_theStatutoryBranch.text: Whenever a person was convicted of one or more misdemeanors committed while such person was under eighteen years of age, and the offense or offenses occurred before January 1, 2000, such person may file a petition with the Superior Court at the location in which such conviction was effected for an order of erasure, and the Superior Court shall direct all police and court records and records of the state's or prosecuting attorney pertaining to such case to be erased.
conditionsItImposes: committed while under eighteen years of age
petition filed with the Superior Court at the location in which the conviction was effected
conditionsItDoesNotImpose: no bar for pending criminal charges
part1_theStatutoryBranch.theCourtHasNoDiscretion: The Superior Court 'shall direct' erasure. This is a duty on the stated facts, not a grant-or-deny discretion.
part1_theStatutoryBranch.subsectionFHasTwoBranches: (f)(1) is the automatic branch for under-eighteen misdemeanours committed on or after January 1, 2000 and before July 1, 2012, erased by operation of law or actual erasure. (f)(2) is the petition branch for offences before January 1, 2000. They are preserved separately and must not be collapsed: the automatic branch's settled strategy does not carry over.

part2_whatTheFormItselfSays.readFrom: the retained official binary, not a description of it
part2_whatTheFormItselfSays.title: PETITION FOR CLEAN SLATE ERASURE, CONVICTIONS BEFORE 1/1/2000
part2_whatTheFormItselfSays.itsOwnLimitingInstruction: Instruction 1 reads: 'Only use this form to ask the court to erase convictions for offenses committed before January 1, 2000 that are eligible for erasure under Clean Slate.' The word is 'only', and the qualifier is Clean Slate eligibility, not the date alone.
theSwornRepresentationsItRequires: the crimes happened before January 1, 2000 and fall in the erasable categories (misdemeanours, class D or E felonies, unclassified felonies or motor-vehicle violations carrying no more than five years)

the crimes are not blocked from erasure, the blocks including repeat § 14-227a violations within ten years, sexually violent crimes, nonviolent sexual crimes and the crimes listed in § 54-142a(e)(2)(C)
waiting period: for misdemeanours, no other conviction within seven years of the last conviction; for felonies, ten years

sentence completion: imprisonment, parole, special parole, transitional supervision and probation completed, both for the crimes to be erased and for any other crime convicted of in state court on or after January 1, 2000
part2_whatTheFormItselfSays.howItIsExecuted: sworn under oath before a Notary Public, Commissioner of the Superior Court, Clerk or other proper officer, under a certification that a deliberate false statement may result in criminal charges.
part2_whatTheFormItselfSays.itsOrderBlock: The court's block on page 1 offers 'Denied' or 'Granted, as to the following convictions'.

part3_theLegalDistinctionTested.theTest: Whether JD-CR-202's ordinary Clean Slate conditions would improperly add requirements to the § 54-142a(f)(2) route.
part3_theLegalDistinctionTested.result: They would, in four ways, and the conflict is not marginal.
addedRequirements: A seven-year clean period. (f)(2) imposes none. A person who qualifies under (f)(2) but has a later conviction could not truthfully sign paragraph 2.
Sentence completion, including for unrelated post-2000 convictions. (f)(2) imposes none.
No pending state criminal charges. (f)(2) imposes none.
The excluded-offence list, including the § 54-142a(e)(2)(C) crimes. (f)(2) reaches 'one or more misdemeanors' without that list.
part3_theLegalDistinctionTested.theFormCannotEvenRecordTheStatutoryTrigg: JD-CR-202 has no field for the petitioner's age at the time of the offence. Being under eighteen when the offence was committed is (f)(2)'s defining element, and the form provides nowhere to state it. A form that cannot record the fact the statute turns on is not that statute's vehicle.
part3_theLegalDistinctionTested.aFifthDifference: The form directs filing where the petitioner was sentenced; (f)(2) says the location in which the conviction was effected. Usually the same place, not necessarily.
part3_theLegalDistinctionTested.aSixthDifference: The form's order block is grant-or-deny. (f)(2) says the court shall direct erasure.
part3_theLegalDistinctionTested.whyThisMattersMoreThanFit: Using the form would put a petitioner under oath to conditions the statute does not require, on a certification that a deliberate false statement may be charged criminally. That is worse than an imperfect fit; it is a sworn statement the participant may be unable to make and does not need to make.

theFourPossibleAnswers: 1. JD-CR-202 is the accepted or required vehicle for (f)(2) - NOT established, and the form's own instruction points the other way.
2. another official form controls - NOT established. No such form was found.
3. no official form controls and a custom petition is accepted - NOT established. No source read says a custom petition is accepted.
4. the branch has been superseded or absorbed - NOT established. (f)(2) is current statutory text.
part4_whatWasSearchedForAndNotFound.theRetainedConnecticutInventoryHoldsNoCa: The retained Connecticut source set contains exactly three documents: JD-CR-202 itself, the DPS-0846-C criminal-history record request, and the source-gated DESPP-0847-C hearing form for post-1/1/2000 Clean Slate erasure. None is an under-eighteen or pre-2000 erasure petition other than JD-CR-202.
part4_whatWasSearchedForAndNotFound.whatCouldNotBeRead: This environment's egress proxy blocks jud.ct.gov, cga.ct.gov, law.justia.com, codes.findlaw.com and lawserver.com. Judicial Branch form instructions, self-help pages, Practice Book provisions, standing orders, clerk filing guidance and the authoritative form inventory could therefore not be read directly. The form itself was read from the retained binary, and the statutory text from search results quoting it.
part4_whatWasSearchedForAndNotFound.whyThatMattersToTheAnswer: It does not change the negative finding about JD-CR-202, which rests on the form's own retained bytes. It is the reason the positive question stays open: an express Judicial Branch statement that some vehicle governs (f)(2) may exist and simply was not reachable from here.

part5_theCurrentImplementation.whatTheOwnerAdoptedRecordSays: data/rcap-grade-a/legal-decisions/BATCH_ADOPTION_PACKAGE_2026-09-02.json carries two separate obligation units for this family. The automatic branch, obligation:unit:CT:ct-under18-misdemeanor:ct-under18-misdemeanor-branch-automatic, is an explicit_legal_design_unit. The petition branch, obligation:unit:CT:ct-under18-misdemeanor:ct-under18-misdemeanor-branch-petition, is unit_unavailable with the reason 'The current form or accepted custom pleading is unresolved, as is the historical offense-date and classification rule. The automatic branch's settled strategy does not carry over to this branch.' Both carry runtimePathwayId null and runtimeRouteId null.
part5_theCurrentImplementation.soTheBranchIsAlreadyBlocked: (f)(2) is wired to no runtime route and claims no vehicle. That is the correct current state and this record does not change it.
part5_theCurrentImplementation.theConflictIsNotWhereItWasExpected: Neither the compiled Connecticut profile nor the CT packet specification maps JD-CR-202 to (f)(2). The profile contains zero occurrences of 'under eighteen', 'under 18', 'before January 1, 2000' or '54-142a(f)', and every JD-CR-202 rule in it is framed as Clean Slate. The specification's own label is 'Petitioned Clean Slate erasure for eligible pre-2000 convictions (JD-CR-202)'. Both are correctly scoped.
part5_theCurrentImplementation.whatIsActuallyWrong: One compiled routing rule states the JD-CR-202 rule without the Clean Slate qualifier its siblings carry. rule-08-for-convictions-entered-before-1-1-2000-the-person-file has sourceConditionText 'for convictions entered BEFORE 1/1/2000 the person files petition JD-CR-202 with the sentencing court', conditions on case_outcome convicted_other and court only, and names no eligibility, waiting period, offence level or age. Its sibling rule-23 carries the qualifier: 'Eligible conviction, pre-2000 Clean Slate by petition JD-CR-202, sentencing 7 / 10 yrs'. An under-eighteen pre-2000 misdemeanant is a pre-2000 conviction, so the unqualified rule describes them.
part5_theCurrentImplementation.whatWasNotProven: Whether rule-08 actually causes such a participant to land on the JD-CR-202 route. It is a pathway_routing rule offering four candidate pathways, and the evaluation-stage route rule additionally requires offense_level, offense_category, pardon_status and sentence_completion_date. Establishing the live effect needs an evaluator run against a purpose-built Connecticut under-eighteen answer set, which was not built here.
part5_theCurrentImplementation.exposure: The JD-CR-202 route rule carries paymentAllowed true, so this is a selling route. That raises the stakes of the unqualified rule and is the reason it is recorded rather than left to be rediscovered.

whatThisRecordDoesNotDo.noFormApproved: JD-CR-202 is not approved for (f)(2) by inference, and no other form is mapped to it.
whatThisRecordDoesNotDo.noCustomPleadingFabricated: No custom petition was drafted or authorised for (f)(2). No source read states that a custom petition is accepted.
whatThisRecordDoesNotDo.noBranchCollapsed: The (f)(1) automatic branch and the (f)(2) petition branch remain separate, and the automatic branch's strategy is not carried into the petition branch.
whatThisRecordDoesNotDo.noRouteChanged: rule-08 was measured, not edited. The Clean Slate route, its rules and its payment state are untouched: changing a selling route is a route change this record does not authorise.
whatThisRecordDoesNotDo.noAdjacentCtRouteReviewed: Cannabis erasure, ordinary post-2000 Clean Slate, pardon routes and unrelated under-eighteen relief were not reviewed. The cannabis and pardon rows were read only far enough to confirm they are distinct rows.

statusOfThisRecord.readThisFirst: This is a form-identity determination. It resolves one question negatively, leaves the positive question open, changes no specification and opens no route.

remainingReview: Two things, and they are separable. First, the (f)(2) vehicle itself: an authoritative Connecticut Judicial Branch source - form instructions, a self-help page, a Practice Book provision, a standing order, clerk filing guidance or the form inventory - stating what a person files under § 54-142a(f)(2). None was reachable from this environment. Second, whether rule-08's unqualified pre-2000 routing actually lands an under-eighteen petitioner on JD-CR-202, which needs an evaluator run against a purpose-built answer set.
